study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To integrate REACT (Receptor-Enriched Analysis of functional Connectivity by Targets) with normative modeling to derive functional networks enriched with main modulatory, excitatory, and inhibitory neurotransmitter systems, and examine clinical and functional similarity within and across patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and ADHD, linking symptomatology to functional deviations from normality transdiagnostically.

Summary metrics: mean deviation across all ROIs for each subject and molecular system.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The manuscript describes that deviation scores were computed as the difference between predicted and observed molecular-enriched FC values, normalized by prediction uncertainty. These represent z-scores quantifying how much an individual deviates from normative ranges. Summary metrics averaging across ROIs were also computed.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Specifically, we computed a deviation score for each brain ROI, which describes the difference between the predicted molecular-enriched FC and the true molecular-enriched FC, normalised by the prediction uncertainty. ... These deviations, represented as either positive or negative values, indicate how much a subject's molecular-enriched FC for a specific brain region deviates from the established normative FC model derived from healthy controls. ... We also collapsed down the deviation scores of each molecular-enriched network to provide a single mean deviation score for each subject across ROIs.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Between-group comparisons of deviation scores using 1×4 ANOVAs (FSL PALM, 2000 permutations, FDR correction) with lower-level t-tests; 1×4 ANOVAs on summary mean deviation metrics with Tukey HSD post-hoc tests; Binary logistic regression for classification with ROC/AUC metrics; Between-subject correlation matrices for deviation similarity; Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests comparing within-group similarity distributions; Non-parametric repeated measures ANOVAs (Friedman test) with Conover's post-hoc and Bonferroni correction for within- vs between-group similarity; Pearson correlations between transdiagnostic similarity and mean deviation scores, and between transdiagnostic similarity and symptom PCs (Bonferroni correction p<0.05/30); Mass univariate regression analyses (PALM, 2000 permutations, FDR correction) for deviation-symptom mapping linking deviation scores to four symptom-based principal components.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of molecular-enriched functional networks revealed transdiagnostic similarities across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and ADHD, with glutamatergic and GABAergic systems implicated in SCHZ and BPD (suggesting E/I imbalance), cholinergic system in SCHZ, and minimal ADHD-specific alterations; deviations mapped onto transdiagnostic symptom dimensions (psychotic, depressive, inattentive, motor impulsive symptoms) through VAChT- and mGluR5-enriched networks.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative HBR models explained moderate variance in molecular-enriched networks comparable to prior structural studies. Between-group analyses showed significant deviations in VAChT-enriched networks (SCHZ vs HC) and mGluR5-enriched networks (SCHZ and BPD vs HC), with FC values generally lower than normative ranges. Mean summary deviation metrics for mGluR5 distinguished SCHZ from HC (AUC=0.75) and BPD from HC (AUC=0.66), while GABA-A metrics distinguished SCHZ from HC (AUC=0.73). ADHD showed no significant differences from controls in any molecular system. Within-group deviation similarity was significantly higher for SCHZ and BPD compared to HC across all molecular systems, while ADHD showed intermediate similarity. Transdiagnostic similarity was negatively correlated with mean deviation burden for NAT, SERT, mGluR5, and GABA-A systems. PCA of 28 symptom measures yielded 4 components (57.3% variance): PC1 (general psychopathology), PC2 (psychotic/depressive/inattentive/impulsive dysregulation), PC3 (mania), PC4 (cognitive complexity). Transdiagnostic similarity in SERT, VAChT, and mGluR5 systems correlated positively with PC2 scores. Mass univariate regression revealed PC2 negatively correlated with VAChT-enriched FC deviations (bilateral insula, opercular regions, left mid-cingulate, SMA, precuneus) and mGluR5-enriched FC deviations (bilateral insula, opercular regions, STG, cuneus, left lingual, bilateral mid-cingulate, SMA), indicating lower FC in these networks associated with higher transdiagnostic symptom burden. Normative modeling revealed more robust results than conventional REACT analyses without normative framework.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Use of group-average molecular templates acquired in separate healthy subjects with different methodologies resulting in resolution differences; moderate collinearity between some molecular systems (though VIF<5); cross-sectional design limiting causal inference; relatively small clinical sample sizes requiring replication in larger, more diverse cohorts; lack of external validation dataset for deviation-symptom mapping; inability to exclude treatment effects on deviations (patients not drug-naive/drug-free)
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: As with all molecular-enriched network analyses, we utilise group average molecular templates acquired in separate healthy subjects. ... it is important to acknowledge these templates were acquired in separate subjects and using different methodologies, resulting in differences in resolution despite being normalised into the same space. Several of these molecular enriched-networks also show moderate collinearity ... The cross-sectional nature of our data also confines us to observe associations rather than establishing causal relationships ... the sample sizes of the clinical cohorts utilised here were relatively small ... we only tested our deviation-symptom mapping in one dataset. ... we cannot exclude the possibility that treatment within the clinical cohorts may impact the estimation of deviations ... Future studies examining drug-naïve populations ... will be important moving forward.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Study innovatively combined molecular-enriched network analysis (REACT) with normative modeling to link symptoms to neurotransmitter system dysfunction amenable to pharmacological intervention. Molecular templates included transporters for neuromodulatory systems (NAT, DAT, SERT, VAChT) and receptors for excitatory/inhibitory systems (mGluR5, GABA-A) from independent PET/SPECT datasets. REACT two-step GLM approach: (1) spatial regression of molecular templates against fMRI to extract dominant fluctuations per system, (2) regression of these timeseries against voxel-wise BOLD to produce molecular-enriched FC maps. Transdiagnostic approach used PCA to identify symptom dimensions across diagnostic boundaries rather than relying solely on categorical diagnoses. Findings suggest potential for future biomarker development linking brain phenotypes to mechanistically-targeted treatments, particularly cholinergic compounds (e.g., xanomeline) for psychotic symptoms in SCHZ.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is the first study to combine molecular-enriched functional network analysis (REACT) with normative modeling. The study addresses two major barriers in psychiatric neuroimaging: multiscale organization of the brain and clinical heterogeneity. Patients were not drug-naive or drug-free; stable medications were permitted (supplementary materials L149-L151). Diagnostic criteria followed DSM-IV using SCID-I supplemented by Adult ADHD Interview. Quality assurance for diagnostic interviews included minimum kappa 0.75 for overall agreement, sensitivity, specificity, and 0.85 for diagnostic accuracy (supplementary materials L196-L197). The study included deep phenotyping with 28 symptom/trait measures transdiagnostically. Molecular templates were resampled to 2mm³ and normalized 0-1, with reference regions set to minimum GM values. VIF analysis confirmed acceptable collinearity (all <5). Only ROIs with positive explained variance were retained for subsequent analyses (319/443 for NAT, 307/443 for DAT, 296/443 for SERT, 257/443 for VAChT, 418/443 for mGluR5, 421/443 for GABA-A). Sensitivity analyses showed conventional REACT without normative modeling yielded no significant between-group differences and fewer deviation-symptom relationships (SI-Fig 7).
